Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Conversation, family & daily routines · Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

stuck adjective

caught fast

also get stuck, be stuck, jammed

classical

Phaedr. 4.9.12: haerentem vadō
Plaut. Capt. 3.3.17: quid māchiner? quid comminīscar? haereō (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 108, 386

haereō, haerēre, haesī, haesum

verb, second conjugation

be stuck, stick fast; be stuck for what to do

Latin says it with the verb: haereō, I’m stuck. Also of a small child stuck on the shapes of the letters (haesit circā fōrmās litterārum, Quint. 1.1.21).

Examples

  • tum vulpēcula ēvāsit puteō nīxa celsīs cornibus hircumque clausō līquit haerentem vadō

    then the little fox climbed out of the well on his tall horns and left the goat stuck in the waterPhaedr. 4.9.10–12

  • ego stirpem ingentem, vestīgiō pedis ejus haerentem, revellī

    I pulled out a huge thorn stuck in the sole of his footGell. 5.14.22

  • obstipuī, steteruntque comae et vōx faucibus haesit

    I froze, my hair stood on end, and my voice stuck in my throatVerg. A. 2.774

  • Pila in arbore haeret.

    The ball’s stuck in the tree.composed

Other words

  • haesitō, haesitāre, haesitāvī, haesitātum — stick fast (in mud, in shallows)

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.19.2 (Lewis & Short); Ter. Phorm. 780: in eōdem lutō haesitās

    Rare in this literal sense, and not in Cicero, who uses it for “hesitate”.

See also adhere.

SourcesLewis & Short: haereo · Lewis & Short: haesito
